content: 1. Administer norethindrone acetate orally at a dose of 5 mg up to 15 mg per day for a duration of 6 to 9 months. Use in pre-menarche individuals is not recommended due to lack of safety and efficacy data. 2. Acitretin reduces the effectiveness of norethindrone acetate through an unknown mechanism. This combination is contraindicated as it may result in contraceptive failure. 3. Apalutamide decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for reduced therapeutic effects and adjust the dose as per prescribing information. 4. Belzutifan reduces the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. When used with hormonal contraceptives, there is a risk of contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding. Advise females of reproductive potential to use effective non-hormonal contraception. Based on animal studies, belzutifan may cause fetal harm. 5. Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefits outweigh the risks. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable for effective birth control when coadministered. Concomitant use may increase the incidence of menstrual-related adverse effects, such as amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, or menorrhagia. 6. Hormonal contraceptives are not reliable for effective birth control when coadministered. Concomitant use may increase the risk of menstrual-related adverse effects, including amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, or menorrhagia. 7. Coadministration may increase the risk of adverse effects associated with CYP3A4 substrates. 8. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for increased effects and consider dose adjustments. 10. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable for effective birth control when coadministered. Concomitant use may increase the risk of menstrual-related adverse effects, such as amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, or menorrhagia. 11. Mavacamten decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Progestin and ethinyl estradiol are CYP3A4 substrates, and mavacamten may reduce their systemic exposure, leading to contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding. Advise patients to use a contraceptive method unaffected by CYP450 enzyme induction, such as an intrauterine system, or add non-hormonal contraception during coadministration and for 4 months after the last mavacamten dose. 12. Hormonal contraceptives are unreliable for effective birth control when coadministered. Concomitant use may increase the risk of menstrual-related adverse effects, such as amenorrhea, dysmenorrhea, or menorrhagia. 20. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concomitant use with CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose according to product labeling. 21. Norethindrone acetate decreases the effects of albiglutide by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 22. Atazanavir and norethindrone acetate may mutually decrease each other's effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 23. Cenobamate decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Increase the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as needed when coadministered with cenobamate. 24. Clobazam decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by weakly inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive effectiveness may be diminished. Additional non-hormonal contraception is recommended. 25. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 26. Elagolix decreases the levels of norethindrone acetate by weak-to-moderate induction of CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor CYP3A substrates if coadministered and consider increasing their dose if needed. 27. Injectable exenatide may reduce the extent and rate of absorption of oral contraceptives due to its effect on slowing gastric emptying. Advise patients to take oral contraceptives at least 1 hour before exenatide administration. 28. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Adjust the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as necessary. 29. Iloperidone increases the levels of norethindrone acetate by time-dependent inhibition of CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Elevated plasma levels of drugs eliminated by CYP3A4 may occur. 30. Norethindrone acetate decreases the effects of insulin degludec, insulin aspart, and inhaled insulin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor. Progestins may impair glucose tolerance. 31. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate at higher doses (40 mg/day) by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 32. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Lenacapavir may increase CYP3A4 substrate levels initiated within 9 months after the last subcutaneous dose, increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 33. Norethindrone acetate decreases the effects of liraglutide by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance, reducing the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 34. Norethindrone acetate increases the levels of maraviroc by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for potential increased toxicity. 35. Mifepristone decreases the effects of norethindrone acetate by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor. A backup contraceptive method is recommended. 36. Rucaparib increases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Adjust the dosage of CYP3A4 substrates if clinically indicated. 37. Rufinamide decreases the effects of norethindrone acetate by weakly inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Rufinamide may reduce the exposure of drugs that are CYP3A4 substrates. 38. Siltuximab may restore CYP450 enzymatic activity by inhibiting IL-6, which is downregulated during infection and inflammation. Use caution if coadministered with CYP substrates that have a narrow therapeutic index. 39. Stiripentol inhibits and induces CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially altering the effects of norethindrone acetate. Monitor CYP3A4 substrates for increased or decreased effects and adjust dosages as needed. 40. Tazemetostat decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 41. Tecovirimat decreases the levels or effects of norethindrone acetate by weakly inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor sensitive CYP3A4 substrates for effectiveness if coadministered.
